families.rationale: Uniform random graph G(n,p); the reference regime with no structure to exploit. p is kept in the sparse half so a random partition stays near 1/2 and the objective is not nearly saturated.

Exactly d-regular graphs, so the degree sequence carries no signal at all: whatever a solver finds comes from the arrangement, not from hub structure. d in {3,4,5} is the classic hard band for Max-Cut.

Preferential attachment gives a heavy-tailed degree distribution and high-degree hubs; a solver that only reasons about average degree is penalised. m in {2,3,5} spans mean degree about 4 to about 10.

Community structure where a non-trivial partition is known to the generator. p_in/p_out ratios of 4-7x make the structure real but not readable off a degree histogram; the label permutation is random so the partition cannot be inferred from the community sizes alone.

notes: dev and eval draw `reps` independent instances from every (family, stratum) cell; the role is part of the sha256 seed derivation, so no two graphs in the suite share a stream.
calibration draws one instance per (family, stratum) cell, i.e. 12 graphs, and enters no algorithmic selection (INTERFACE.md section 9).
Probability parameters are exact rationals (p_num/p_den); the decimal spelling is display only.
Changing master_seed (or any param) produces a different suite with the same procedure: `build --master-seed N --suite <other dir>`.

identity: graph identity = sha256 of the canonical bytes of <role>/<graph_id>.json; generator.seed is provenance only and no verdict may reference it (INTERFACE.md §2)

roles.calibration: resource-rate calibration only (INTERFACE.md §9); MUST NOT be used for any algorithmic selection
roles.dev: visible development instances; may inform development work
roles.eval: frozen hold-out; evaluated once at the end, never injected into an agent workspace

separation.sampling: dev, eval and calibration are independent draws: each (role, family, stratum, rep) slot gets its own sha256-derived stream keyed by the role
